whatChanged.theRefusalCause: STATED FROM THE RULE AND THE CAPTION, MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED. decideBinding in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs tries the field NAME first and the printed LABEL only if the name matches nothing, and it returned { writable: false, reason: 'no_allowlisted_fact_matches' } on every one of the three subjects available to it: the field name 'ApplicantStreetNumberAndStreetNameLine1'; the CAPTURED caption 'Street Number And Street Name, Including Apartment Or Unit N'; and the caption the pinned form actually prints, 'Street Number And Street Name, Including Apartment Or Unit Number If Applicable'. descriptorsMatching returns [] for all three because participant.street_address requires one of street addr | mailing addr | addr line N | ^addr | address and none of the three carries any of those tokens, while participant.full_legal_name would match on 'Applicant'/'Name' and is correctly refused by its own \bstreet\b clause. An explicitMappings entry cannot reach it either: decideBinding returns on the empty match set BEFORE it consults explicitMappings, confirmed by running it both ways. So this was never a protected-category refusal and never a wrong-caption refusal; it is a gap in the shared descriptor list, and the family-local caption correction below does not close it.

The correction is made anyway, for truth rather than for effect, and the write is carried by a named channel instead.
